answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before it may submit jobs, then slash that bond when independent audits prove fraud. A ridge of repeated claims backed by one operator is no longer free to create: every extra identity ties up capital, and detected abuse destroys it. A pearl of trusted history can lower limits gradually, while cedar-framed audit rules keep the same evidence standard for newcomers and established agents. This raises the cost of Sybils without pretending bonds prevent them outright.
